newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper, aluminium stocks seen falling - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, aluminium stocks seen falling - trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper and aluminium stocks are seen falling later on Friday while copper shipments from China to Singapore warehouses have dried up, base metal traders said.
Copper stocks will probably dip by between 1,000-4,000 tonnes while aluminium inventories are expected to fall by 4,000-6,000 tonnes, the traders said.
"The general consensus of the trade is for a fall of about 3,000-4,000 tonnes," a dealer at a Japanese metal firm said.
"My feeling is 1,000-2,000 tonnes down," another dealer for a Singapore-based metal trading company added.
But metal broker Brandeis was more cautious, saying in its daily review that LME copper stock movements are likely to "range between a rise of 1,000 tonnes and a fall of 3,000-4,000 tonnes."
On aluminium, Singapore dealers said there should be a further drawdown in stocks when the LME report is issued at 0900 GMT on Friday.
"It will be 4,000 tonnes down," a dealer for a Japanese trading house said.
Another trader said, however, that "it could go down by 5,000-6,000 tonnes."
Traders said that further copper shipments from China appear to have stopped. Some 5,000 tonnes of Chinese metal were estimated to have arrived here early last week.
"We didn't see any more copper from China being unloaded here," one trader said.
The quantity of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 56,025 tonnes last Tuesday, down 450 tonnes from the level of the previous Friday.
Three month copper prices were quoted by regional dealers at 0230 GMT at US$2,386/91 a tonne compared with the late quote in London on Thursday of $2,390/94 a tonne.
Aluminium prices were seen at $1,647/52 a tonne at 0230 GMT against the late quote in London yesterday of $1,649/51 a tonne and the LME kerb close on Thursday of $1,652, traders said.
